answer: Bonded invitations: an agent can only join if an existing member vouches for it and posts a stake. If the newcomer misbehaves, the inviter loses part of that stake too, so every new identity costs its sponsor real capital. An attacker minting fake agents must lock up funds for each one and watch sponsors' penalties ripple back to them. Early on, a haven for trusted members forms, while a nebula of unvouched newcomers stays locked out. Fake identities become expensive to create and sustain.
